hard_failures.finding: Family-of-statements quantifier domain. quantifiers.formal (lines 48-50) and conclusion.statement_formal (line 219) both range 'forall (s,delta) in D0', and D0 (line 58) is defined as 'Sobolev variant s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1), or the smooth-with-decay default'; the disjunction is mirrored in regularity.data_regularity (line 149). The named topology differs per disjunct (genericity.ambient_space, line 164: weighted Sobolev product H^s_delta x H^{s-1}_{delta+1}; line 165: Frechet topology for the smooth-with-decay class), and genericity.is_part_of_class is true, so one class_id currently denotes one statement in a Banach/Sobolev setting and one in a Frechet setting. No transfer lemma between the two readings exists anywhere in the artifact. The falsifier semantics split with the domain: tier_1 (lines 256-263) refutes the class by exhibiting one (s,delta) in D0 with a non-meager extendible set, so a single-regularity counterexample would refute the whole class and leave the other disjunct untouched. The artifact and the taxonomy call the Sobolev setting a 'registered Sobolev variant' (artifacts/formulation/formulation_taxonomy.yaml#class_contracts.AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN.data_class_freeze), but VARIANT_REGISTRY.json contains no Sobolev/data-class variant registration (registry variant_ids: SET, CH, DISTRIBUTIONAL, H2LOC, TWOSIDED, L2CONN, LIP), and canonical F0 lists only [SET, CH]. The claimed registration therefore does not exist, and the disjunction is carried inside the class quantifier instead of outside it.
